entries.label: t3code/group/thread-picker
entries.note:
GROUP entry, built from stack/thread-picker.toml. These PRs all
edit the same CommandPalette trio, so combining them here -- against upstream
main -- resolves the combination once against a STABLE base instead of
re-deriving it against a shifting assembled stack on every refresh.

It also gives the add-project flow helpers a home: they are what the group needs
to coexist, so they live on the group branch rather than as a stack epilogue.

Rebuild the group first, then pin its new head here.

entries.summary: Refresh a project favicon when its icon is clicked
Recover stranded provider turns after lost completion events
Keep the Android new-task composer above the keyboard while it expands
Clone a thread through its latest completed response from the sidebar
User-local project icons
Self-heal empty thread details and back off failed thread subscriptions
Recover subscriptions that lose their transport
entries.note:
Adjacent to #4405: both edit packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/client.ts and its
test, and this is the only other topic that touches subscription lifecycle.

A durable subscription that dies with a transport error drains and waits for a
session the supervisor never produces unless the socket reports closed, so the
environment silently stops updating until the client restarts. Root cause behind
#4589; #4593 only recovers the settle path.

entries.summary: Recover draft thread IDs after failed bootstrap cleanup
entries.note:
Under applyPatches this needed a compat patch because
OrchestrationGetSnapshotError and OrchestrationDispatchCommandError have
byte-identical bodies, so `patch` silently landed retryWithNewThreadId on the
WRONG class at this stack's offset. A 3-way merge cannot make that mistake.

entries.label: t3code/local/nix-flake
entries.summary: Nix flake: dev shell and desktop package
entries.note:
Purely additive (flake.nix + nix/README.md), so it carries at essentially zero
conflict cost -- the ideal shape for a permanent-carry topic. Upstream
CONTRIBUTING says they are not accepting contributions and want an issue first,
so this is carried locally rather than opened as a cold PR.

entries.label: t3code/client-suite
entries.summary: Complete client-only desktop, pairing, environment presentation, and settings suite
entries.note:
Canonical cumulative client branch. Subsumes #4444, #4474, #4496, #4505,
#4538, #4548, #4559, #4567, the branch-linked
t3code/show-remote-host-name topic, and the diagnostics work from #4486.
Thread host badges are client-local presentation, default on for every
environment (including localhost), and do not depend on classifying the app as
a local owner or remote client.

entries.label: t3code/unify-environment-selection
entries.summary: Align settings ownership and environment selection across settings pages
entries.note:
Places the shared environment selector inside the Environment navigation group
and repeats it in a clearly labeled scope strip on environment-owned pages.
Keybindings are client-owned and client-persisted; Connections remains a
client page. Assistant output and new-thread/worktree defaults are client-owned
across web, desktop, and mobile. Provider configuration, host paths, source
control, and diagnostics remain environment-owned.

entries.summary: Reconcile client state when a settle does not land
entries.note:
Placed last among the client-runtime subscription topics: it adds a
`resync-requested` wakeup and merges a request stream into the web wakeups
layer, so it touches apps/web/src/connection/platform.ts after both
t3code/client-suite and t3code/unify-environment-selection have restructured
it. Its one-line filter change in client-runtime state/threads.ts sits in a
different region than #4405's subscription backoff. Reported as #4589.

entries.label: t3code/local/build-provenance
entries.summary: Show the build's commit, and a Settings page describing the assembled stack
entries.note:
Reads stack-build-info.json, which the rebuild writes as this branch's final
commit, so it has to be able to see the assembled result -- but it is ordinary
app code and belongs on a topic, not in the tooling. Placed last so its edits
to SettingsPanels.tsx and SettingsSidebarNav.tsx land after t3code/client-suite
and t3code/unify-environment-selection have finished restructuring them.

Local rather than a PR: the value is entirely in describing a personally
assembled stack, which upstream does not have.

entries.summary: Clear pending approval and user-input requests when no provider session is bound
entries.note:
Four carried topics touch its two files: #4386 and #4390 edit
ProviderCommandReactor.ts, #4427 and #4506 edit session-logic.test.ts. Appended
so it merges once against their final assembled state rather than being
re-resolved as each lands. Its own hunks are small: a helper beside
stalePendingRequestDetail plus two `detail:` lines on the server, one test
inside the derivePendingUserInputs describe on the web.

Branched from upstream a17cbc3b4, which is newer than the lock's recorded
upstream, so this entry wants a refresh rather than a reproduce.
